quotes.text: Learn how to accept Afterpay (also known as Clearpay in the UK), a payment method in the US, CA, UK, AU, and NZ.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: A Checkout Session must satisfy all of the following conditions to support Afterpay payments:

If they take no action within 3 hours, the [PaymentMethod](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/object.md) detaches and the object status for the [PaymentIntent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/object.md) automatically transitions to `requires_payment_method`.

Stripe cancels the PaymentIntent and sends a [payment_intent.canceled](https://docs.stripe.com/api/events/types.md#event_types-payment_intent.canceled) event if the payment isn’t captured during the 7-day window.
You then have up to 13 days after authorization to capture the rest of the payment.

findings: The 2026-11-07 new raw is an index, not a detailed integration variant: new raw lines 9-21 route Checkout, Elements via Checkout Sessions or Payment Intents, Direct API, iOS, Android and React Native. The giant content.diff lines 3-15 and 2872-2880 reflects replacement of a bundled multi-variant capture by navigation, not demonstrated retirement of the older flows.

The 2026-05-06 old raw documents Checkout one-time/domestic-currency limits and payment mode only at old raw lines 18-35; account eligibility at 16; Checkout Session creation at 43-49. Elements Checkout Sessions server/client roles and a 24-hour Session expiry are at 280-284, and Payment Intents server/client secret/confirmation roles at 967-978 and 1095-1102. The new index does not revalidate those details.

The current source only pins the old raw at source lines 6-7 and lists three paths at 13 and 19. The new index explicitly has four web variant routes—Checkout, Elements Checkout Sessions, Elements Payment Intents, and Direct API—plus iOS, Android and React Native at new raw lines 13-21. The source must acknowledge or route the separately listed Direct API and mobile variants, not offer its three paths as a complete taxonomy; add the new raw as navigation-only provenance. Old mobile branches are at old raw lines 1781-1785, 2129-2133 and 2481-2485.

Baseline summary line 23 says PaymentIntents in requires_action auto-expire after 3 hours. Old raw lines 217-220 specifically say inactivity after redirect detaches the PaymentMethod and returns the PaymentIntent to requires_payment_method, while the error table at 231 describes unsuccessful authorization after initial checkout creation as expiry. The summary's unqualified auto-expire wording obscures the state transition and different clock anchors; this is an existing-summary correction, not a new raw delta.

Old raw lines 189-199 distinguish checkout.session.completed authorization from payment_intent.succeeded payment success and payment_intent.payment_failed; old raw lines 1244-1248 and 1722-1730 recommend event/webhook status checks rather than client return. The new index proves no payment execution or eligibility. Context route exists from wiki/index.md:7 to wiki/stripe-index.md:326 and wiki/stripe-index.md:747 to wiki/concepts/stripe-bnpl.md:61-75,256.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/afterpay-clearpay/accept-a-payment, the complete new capture establishes Afterpay/Clearpay identity, five named countries and seven variant routes only: four web routes comprising Checkout, two Elements API routes and Direct API, plus three mobile routes (new raw lines 5-21). It states no account eligibility, request parameters, API state transitions or payment success. The paired 2026-05-06 guide supplies dated Checkout payment-mode/one-time/domestic-currency requirements (old raw lines 16-35), distinguishes Checkout Sessions from Payment Intents and server creation from client confirmation (old raw lines 280-284, 967-978, 1095-1102), and separates authorization, success and failure events (old raw lines 189-199). The mapped source-stripe-afterpay-clearpay-accept-payment.md currently lists only three paths, 3-hour handling, billing details and shipping; it fails to acknowledge the separately indexed Direct API and mobile routes and lacks new index provenance (source lines 13-33). No successful payment or merchant eligibility was tested.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/afterpay-clearpay/accept-a-payment, the November capture's change is presentation/navigation: new raw lines 9-21 separately list Checkout, Elements Checkout Sessions, Elements Payment Intents, Direct API, iOS, Android and React Native, while the paired diff removes the old bundled details (diff lines 3-15, 2872-2880). It does not prove deprecation, changed eligibility or newer behavior. Keep source-stripe-afterpay-clearpay-accept-payment.md's May 2026 claims dated; correct its incomplete three-path taxonomy by explicitly routing or acknowledging Direct API and the mobile variants, and correct its broad 3-hour auto-expiry phrasing against PaymentMethod detachment and PaymentIntent requires_payment_method (old raw lines 217-231; source lines 13, 19, 23). Old Elements manual capture says 7 days but legacy Direct API/mobile says 13 days (old raw lines 1262-1266, 1567-1571, 2022-2026), requiring variant-specific reciprocal warnings. The new index says nothing about live SDK versions, server versus client implementation, authorization versus payment success or return-page finality.
